title: Buying his first soprano for Billy May's arrangement
summary: He never owned a soprano until Billy May brought in a soprano part around 1939-40; before that only Hodges and Bechet played it.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: See, I never owned a soprano until Billy May brought an arrangement in back in 1939 or '40, with
a soprano part, and I said, "I haven't got a soprano, Billy." And he said, "Well, go buy one, the part's here." And I did.
And you hadn't played on in all those years?

No. Like I say, they didn't have a very good reputation amongs -- now, my God, everybody's playing them. But even when I started playing it there, I -- besides Johnny Hodges and Sidney Bechet, that's about all there was.
